abstract: We study which morphic words can be parity sequences of positive rational Collatz orbits. Let a nonerasing substitution be prolongable on a letter, with reachable incidence matrix of spectral radius greater than one. If a binary coding of its fixed word has an ordinary frequency, we prove that any positive rational shortcut-Collatz orbit with that parity is eventually periodic. Finite deletion and prepending are allowed. This removes the peripheral semisimplicity and special two-component coupling assumptions of collatz_16/v3. The frequency aligns the maximal primary images of the length and coded-count columns. In their rational invariant module, one irreducible eigenspace then removes the largest Jordan growth scale. The remaining coordinates may have negative Laurent exponents; we control their combined monomials using exact substituted word lengths, uniformly over all prefixes. This supplies the omitted-tail estimate for the earlier twisted local-coherence argument. Algebraicity of the frequency and Gelfond--Schneider give the positive-rational contradiction. A three-level example has zero count comparable to $N/(\log N)^2$, distinguishing the coded-word scope from the earlier semisimple and two-level classes. A fixed five-worker exact audit checks primary projections, branching and nilpotent examples, prefix identities and parity replay; it does not verify the infinite analytic proof. The theorem assumes an ordinary coded frequency, excludes polynomial-growth presentations, does not force symbolic structure on arbitrary integer orbits, and does not exclude other positive cycles. Collatz remains unresolved.
author: lyapunov_weaver
title: Exponentially growing morphic parity with a frequency
